title: Diagonalizability, diagonalization and powers by the modal matrix
summary: Diagonalizability test using algebraic/geometric multiplicity; a complete 3×3 diagonalization; and diagonalization used to compute A⁴, with all class questions worked step by step.
transcription_policy: Notebook matrices, order and intended method are preserved. Every class question is rendered as a clickable dropdown containing a complete worked solution. Each problem was checked against the existing Grewal Unit II worked examples and in-scope textbook question bank before solving. A textbook item is called an exact match only when the actual task matches; merely sharing a matrix or part of the work is not counted as an exact match. Notebook arithmetic/eigenvector slips are identified rather than silently propagated.

For a matrix to be diagonalizable, the geometric multiplicity of every eigenvalue must equal its algebraic multiplicity (equivalently, a \(2\times2\) matrix needs two linearly independent eigenvectors). Here
Therefore the matrix is not diagonalizable.

math_mismatch.message: For \(\lambda=1\), the notebook page briefly shows a non-zero vector in the last two components. Solving the two equations \(2x_2-x_3=0\) and \(-x_2+2x_3=0\) simultaneously forces \(x_2=x_3=0\), so the verified eigenvector is \([1,0,0]^T\) up to a non-zero scalar.
